name: Decapeptide-12
lead: Decapeptide-12 is a ten-amino-acid cosmetic peptide marketed for skin brightening. It is described in the literature as a novel peptide used to lighten hyperpigmentation, and a 2021 pharmaceutics paper characterises it as safer than hydroquinone in reducing melanin content, with efficacy of more than 50% over 16 weeks of twice-daily treatment, but limited by poor skin penetration because it is hydrophilic and large [4].

The human evidence consists of small open-label studies in which it was combined with other products rather than tested alone: a 0.01% decapeptide-12 cream used with an antioxidant cleanser, a glycolic-acid moisturiser or lotion and a broad-spectrum sunscreen [1][2]. No controlled trial isolating the peptide is present among the sources used here.
The sources contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of it.

paras: Decapeptide-12 is used in cosmetic products for photodamage-related hyperpigmentation, melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation [1][2][3].

It is described as a tyrosinase-inhibiting peptide that reduces melanin content [4]. Its hydrophilicity and large molecular size limit transcutaneous penetration, which led researchers to test structural modification, chemical penetration enhancers and microneedles to improve skin retention and permeation [4].

In a prospective open-label study of 15 women (13 completed) with Fitzpatrick skin types I-IV and facial hyperpigmentation from chronic photodamage, decapeptide-12 was used with an antioxidant cleanser, a glycolic-acid moisturiser and sunscreen; at 24 weeks 38.5% of participants had cleared from moderate to no photodamage on the grading scale, 30.7% improved from moderate to mild, and 15.4% moved from severe to moderate and another 15.4% from severe to mild. The treatments were reported to be well tolerated [1].

A multicentre open-label study in 33 Hispanic women with mild to moderate melasma used 0.01% decapeptide-12 with an antioxidant cleanser, 20% buffered glycolic acid lotion and SPF 30 sunscreen for 16 weeks; mean decreases in the MASI score were 36%, 46%, 54% and 60% at weeks 4, 8, 12 and 16, with no adverse events reported [2]. A 2014 report examined combined topical delivery and dermal infusion of the peptide for post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of colour [3].
All of these studies were uncontrolled and tested multi-component systems, so the contribution of the peptide alone cannot be separated from the glycolic acid and sunscreen they included.

card.summary: A cosmetic brightening peptide with only small, uncontrolled, multi-product studies behind it.
card.note: Studies tested it inside a system with glycolic acid and sunscreen, so its own effect is unclear.

quick.overview:
Decapeptide-12 is a short peptide sold in cosmetic brightening products for dark spots, melasma and sun-related pigmentation. Small open-label studies report improvement in melasma scores and photodamage grades.

Those studies used a full routine including glycolic acid and sunscreen and had no control group.
quick.mechanism: It is described as inhibiting tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes melanin, and has been reported to reduce melanin content. Its size and water solubility limit how well it penetrates skin.
quick.risks: The open-label studies reported good tolerability and no adverse events in the small groups tested. Long-term safety data and independent controlled trials were not found in the sources used here.
